messages:
sasha-sre: Heads up — saw steady growth in the KV cache footprint on Dedicated after a 10k-token long-context run. Not an instant leak, more like the reclaim thermostat never triggers.

maria-ops: Oof. Which fleet/instance type? Dedicated or onprem?

sasha-sre: Dedicated GPU pool (p4d-like), but I repro'd on a smaller private on-prem node too. Hosted copies show milder growth.

kevin-ml: Can you paste the short perf sample? Even a few lines help.

sasha-sre: Sure — snippet from the allocator probe during the run:
```
time=00:42:31 kv_cache.total_bytes=12.1G kv_cache.reclaimed=214k kv_cache.evictions=11 kv_cache.coalesce_passes=0
time=00:52:31 kv_cache.total_bytes=13.9G kv_cache.reclaimed=220k kv_cache.evictions=13 kv_cache.coalesce_passes=0
time=01:02:31 kv_cache.total_bytes=15.7G kv_cache.reclaimed=231k kv_cache.evictions=14 kv_cache.coalesce_passes=0
```
Note `coalesce_passes=0` — reclaim loop isn't compacting variable-length page segments.

jamal-eng: Interesting. On Hosted we have a periodic coalesce job that runs with `--kv-coalesce-interval=300s` and a slightly different allocator profile (mimalloc vs jemalloc). Dedicated default config sets interval=0 to avoid noisy compactions.

maria-ops: That config drift could explain differences. Dedicated was tuned to avoid CPU spikes under heavy batching. But if it lets fragments accumulate that's worse.

kevin-ml: Could also be kernel/page mapping differences. On private boxes we saw page folding failures when page alignment didn't match GPU DMA allocations — leads to small orphan spans. Any MTU/NIC offload differences (for VPC) affect scatter?

oliver: Onprem had `rdma` enabled and a custom `hugepage` setup. That historically changed slab behavior. We should check `numa_balancing` and `transparent_hugepage` settings.

infra-bot: Deploy note: dedicated-pool-3 restarted 1759876600 for kernel-5.10 -> 5.15 test, no config change applied.

sasha-sre: Good call. I ran a quick compare: hosted (container) uses kernel 6.x, dedicated nodes stuck on 5.15, onprem varied. The reclaim thread reacts slower on 5.15 in our measurement windows.

jamal-eng: Two parallel actions: (1) flip `--kv-coalesce-interval` from 0 to 120s in a canary on dedicated, (2) collect page map dumps + `pagemap` traces on the onprem repro. Anyone want the canary?

maria-ops: I can push the canary to dedicated-pool-3 after business hours. Set rollout to single-node, increase CPU cap for the coalesce job.

kevin-ml: Also add a lightweight metric: `kv.coalesce.ratio = coalesce_passes / evictions` and alert if < 0.2 over 15m. That'll catch degenerate thermostats.

oliver: For onprem I'll capture `numastat -m` and `cat /sys/kernel/mm/transparent_hugepage/enabled` and send logs.

sasha-sre: Thanks. Last note — batching heuristics interact: larger batch sizes increase allocator churn and produce more small tail allocations in the KV slab. We might need a short-term change: favor smaller batches for very long-context inference (>=8k tokens) to reduce fragmentation density.

jamal-eng: Agreed. I'll add a policy hook: when sequence_length > 8000, cap batch at 4 and force an async coalesce hint after each request.

maria-ops: Schedule: canary tonight, metrics update + alert tomorrow morning, onprem traces by EOD.

sasha-sre: Perfect. Thanks all — will follow up with the traces/graphs once I have them.

infra-bot: Action created: KVC-1273 "thermostat coalesce canary + page dump" assigned -> jamal-eng, due 1759952000

kevin-ml: If this fix looks stable we should bake a profile-guided default: moderate coalesce interval + small-batch when long contexts detected. Saves us surprise rollouts.

sasha-sre: Yup. Adding to postmortem template too.

maria-ops: :thumbsup:
